items.title:
io.tesseraql:tesseraql-s3 0.12.0 发布, Optional S3 (and S3-compatible) object store for attachments (roadmap Phase 30
    slice 2): an S3BlobStore on AWS SDK for Java v2 (Apache-2.0), selected by
    tesseraql.object-storage.provider: s3 and discovered through the BlobStoreProvider ServiceLoader
    (the PdfEngine idiom). One module covers AWS S3 and every compatible store (Cloudflare R2, Ceph,
    Backblaze B2) via endpoint/region/pathStyle/checksumMode. Apps that do not store blobs in S3
    simply omit this jar, so the AWS SDK stays out of their deployment. Integration tests run against
    Adobe S3Mock (Apache-2.0); MinIO is not used (its server is AGPLv3, ch. 50 decision point 6).

io.tesseraql:tesseraql-s3 0.12.0 发布, Optional S3 (and S3-compatible) object store for attachments (roadmap Phase 30
    slice 2): an S3BlobStore on AWS SDK for Java v2 (Apache-2.0), selected by
    tesseraql.object-storage.provider: s3 and discovered through the BlobStoreProvider ServiceLoader
    (the PdfEngine idiom). One module covers AWS S3 and every compatible store (Cloudflare R2, Ceph,
    Backblaze B2) via endpoint/region/pathStyle/checksumMode. Apps that do not store blobs in S3
    simply omit this jar, so the AWS SDK stays out of their deployment. Integration tests run against
    Adobe S3Mock (Apache-2.0); MinIO is not used (its server is AGPLv3, ch. 50 decision point 6).

    deployment; putting it on the classpath is the whole install (ServiceLoader, design
    ch. 28, 47).

se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom 1.0.2 发布, Bill of Materials for the VibeTags annotation processor. Import this BOM to get
        a coherent vibetags-annotations + vibetags-processor pair without specifying
        each version individually.

        Recommended setup — annotations on the compile classpath, processor on the
        annotation-processor path only (the processor jar pulls in slf4j/logback,
        which has no business on consumer code's compileClasspath):

        Maven:
            <dependencyManagement>
                <dependencies>
                    <dependency>
                        <groupId>se.deversity.vibetags</groupId>
                        <artifactId>vibetags-bom</artifactId>
                        <version>1.0.2</version>
                        <type>pom</type>
                        <scope>import</scope>
                    </dependency>
                </dependencies>
            </dependencyManagement>

        Gradle:
            implementation platform('se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom:1.0.2')
            annotationProcessor platform('se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom:1.0.2')
            compileOnly 'se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-annotations'
            annotationProcessor 'se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-processor'

        @AIIgnore, @AIPrivacy, @AICore, @AIPerformance). Zero third-party dependencies.
        All annotations use RetentionPolicy.SOURCE so they leave no trace in the
        consumer's compiled bytecode — this jar exists purely to give javac the
        symbols it needs at compile time.

        Pair this with vibetags-processor on the annotation-processor classpath:

            <dependency>
                <groupId>se.deversity.vibetags</groupId>
